newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says rates DCB Bank B/C individual.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says rates DCB Bank B/C individual.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Tuesday it had assigned an individual rating of B/C and a legal rating of 2 to DCB Bank, the fourth largest Malaysian bank.

"DCB has an adequate overall financial profile but while its profitability is about on par with that of the larger banks, it is less liquid, more inter-bank dependent and less diversified," IBCA said.
"The bank has a concentration in lending to manufacturing companies that accounts for 35.8 percentof its loan book compared to 23.3 percent for the banking industry," IBCA said.
"It has a particular niche in lending to the Malaysian operations of Japanese manufacturing companies due to its ties to a major shareholder, Sakura Bank of Japan," IBCA said.
DCB's controlling shareholder, Rashid Hussain Berhad, has just announced the acquisition of Kwong Yik Bank from Malayan Banking and plans to merge Kwong Yik with DCB, IBCA said.
"The merged entity would still be the fourth largest bank but total assets would rise to about RM30 bln, making it approximately the size of Public Bank," IBCA said.
"Overall, IBCA is of the opinion that the two banks complement each other, and that the merger will be positive for DCB," IBCA said.
The individual rating is assigned based on the pre-merger evaluation of DCB and the agency will review the rating when full details of the merger are available, it said.

A bank's individual rating is an evaluation of its financial strength based on the premise that it is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners, IBCA said.
Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if the rated bank were to run into difficulties, IBCA said.

A legal rating of 2 indicates that, in IBCA's opinion, support would be provided to DCB Bank should it encounter difficulties even though there is no explicit guarantee of support from the government, IBCA said.
Bank Negara, Malaysia's central bank, has a long history of fully supporting banks in difficulties, it said.
